system:
You repair one knowledge atom that auditors sent back. Use only the supplied evidence sentences; add no background knowledge.

Rules for the repaired atoms:
- One independently assessable claim per atom, written as one sentence that is understood without the source.
- If the atom joined several claims, split it into separate atoms (at most 3), most important first.
- Every atom must be fully stated in the evidence sentences it cites. Remove anything the evidence does not state. Keep quantifiers, negation, hedges, and formulas (LaTeX in $...$).
- Remove procedural or evaluative add-ons and stacked conditions; keep a condition only if the claim is false without it.
- Drop attributions such as "the authors state" when the claim itself is general.
- Use the S label that fits: S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends.
- If no valid atom can be written from this evidence, return an empty list and explain in note.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"atoms": [{"statement": "...", "scope": "S1|S2|S3", "evidence_ids": ["..."]}], "note": ""}

CONCEPT: Sub-group

ATOM DPCPP2-C07-S3-01 (S3): Because sub-group forward progress is currently implementation-defined, kernels that must remain portable cannot rely on sub-groups making progress, even though some devices guarantee that all sub-groups within a work-group eventually execute.

EVIDENCE:
[DPCPP2-p0148-s12] However, on some devices, all sub-groups within a work-group are guaranteed to execute (make progress) eventually, which is a cornerstone
[DPCPP2-p0149-s02] This is currently implementation-defined behavior, and so we cannot rely on sub-groups to make progress if we want our kernels to remain portable.

AUDITOR FINDINGS:
- SINGLE_CLAIM: revise — The portable-progress limitation and existence of devices guaranteeing eventual execution are separately assessable. / Joins two claims: that sub-group forward progress is implementation-defined (requiring portable code not to rely on it) and that some devices guarantee it.
- L1_ONLY: revise — Remove the concessive clause about some devices; retain the implementation-defined progress limitation for portable kernels. / Drop the 'even though some devices...' clause to reduce stacked conditions.
